  414  class SingleWriterShmObjectStorage:
  415      """A single-writer, multiple-reader object storage system built on top of a
  416      shared memory ring buffer. Provides key-value storage with automatic memory
  417      management and cross-process serialization support.
  418  
  419      This storage system follows a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) eviction policy
  420      where the oldest objects are automatically freed when memory runs low.
  421      Memory is reclaimed based on reader reference counting - objects are only
  422      freed when all readers have finished accessing them.
  423  
  424      Architecture:
  425      - Single writer process can put(key, value) objects
  426      - Multiple reader processes can get(address, monotonic_id) objects
  427      - Built on SingleWriterShmRingBuffer for efficient shared memory management
  428      - Thread-safe operations with reader synchronization via locks
  429  
  430      Key Features:
  431      - FIFO Eviction: Oldest objects are evicted first when memory is full
  432      - Reference Counting: Objects are only freed when no readers are
  433        accessing them
  434      - Duplicate Key Handling: Existing keys are not overwritten, just
  435        re-referenced
  436      - Customized Serialization: By default uses Msgpack for efficient
  437        serialization of Python objects, but can be extended for custom types
  438      - Cross-Process Safety: Uses shared memory with proper synchronization

33  // resolveFilePath turns a user-supplied path into the absolute filesystem
   34  // path the write should target. Accepts:
   35  //   - absolute paths, used as-is (no containment check)
   36  //   - repo-prefixed paths (e.g. "gortex/internal/foo.go" in multi-repo mode)
   37  //   - paths relative to the single indexer's root (single-repo mode only)
   38  //
   39  // Returns the absolute path, the repo-relative form for session
   40  // bookkeeping, and an error sentinel describing WHY the input was
   41  // rejected when one of the rejection paths fires:
   42  //
   43  //   - errPathUnresolved — empty input, missing indexer, or a multi-repo
   44  //     bare-relative path that doesn't match any registered prefix
   45  //     (no implicit "primary repo", so the daemon refuses to fall
   46  //     through to its process CWD).
   47  //   - errPathEscape — relative or repo-prefixed input that resolves
   48  //     outside the anchor repo's root via `..` segments. Catches
   49  //     `../../etc/passwd` style attempts at the boundary instead of
   50  //     letting them silently land on system files.
   51  //
   52  // Absolute paths bypass containment by design — agents that hand
   53  // over an absolute path own the location.
   54  func (s *Server) resolveFilePath(rawPath string) (absPath, relPath string, err error) {
   55  	if rawPath == "" {
   56  		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%w: path is empty", errPathUnresolved)
   57  	}
   58  
   59  	if filepath.IsAbs(rawPath) {
   60  		abs := filepath.Clean(rawPath)
   61  		return abs, s.repoRelative(abs), nil
   62  	}
   63  
   64  	if s.multiIndexer != nil {
   65  		// Multi-repo mode requires a repo-prefixed path. Bare-relative
   66  		// paths are ambiguous; refuse rather than fall through to the
   67  		// daemon process CWD. With exactly one tracked repo there is no
   68  		// ambiguity — single-repo mode indexes unprefixed paths, so a
   69  		// bare-relative path anchors to the lone repo's root.
   70  		prefix := matchedRepoPrefix(s.multiIndexer, rawPath)
   71  		if prefix == "" {
   72  			if root, ok := s.multiIndexer.RepoRoot(""); ok {
   73> 				abs := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(root, rawPath))
   74  				if !pathContainedIn(abs, root) {
   75  					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %q resolves to %q, outside repo root %q", errPathEscape, rawPath, abs, root)
   76  				}
   77  				abs = worktreeRootedPath(abs, root, s.multiIndexer)
   78  				return abs, rawPath, nil
   79  			}
   80  			prefixes := s.multiIndexer.RepoPrefixes()
   81  			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%w: path %q does not start with a known repo prefix; expected one of: %s/, or an absolute path",
   82  				errPathUnresolved, rawPath, strings.Join(prefixes, "/, "))
   83  		}
   84  		root, ok := s.multiIndexer.RepoRoot(prefix)
   85  		if !ok {
   86  			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%w: repo prefix %q has no root path", errPathUnresolved, prefix)
   87  		}
   88  		// Collision guard for the lone unprefixed repo: its indexed
   89  		// paths are raw relative paths, so one whose first segment
   90  		// equals the repo's own prefix (repo "api" containing
   91  		// api/handlers.go) would be hijacked by the prefix-strip join.
   92  		// Prefer the raw join when that file actually exists.
   93  		if loneRoot, lok := s.multiIndexer.RepoRoot(""); lok && loneRoot == root {
   94  			raw := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(loneRoot, rawPath))
   95  			if pathContainedIn(raw, loneRoot) {
   96  				if _, err := os.Stat(raw); err == nil {
   97  					return worktreeRootedPath(raw, loneRoot, s.multiIndexer), rawPath, nil
   98  				}
   99  			}
  100  		}
  101  		abs := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(root, strings.TrimPrefix(rawPath, prefix+"/")))
  102  		if !pathContainedIn(abs, root) {
  103  			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %q resolves to %q, outside repo root %q", errPathEscape, rawPath, abs, root)
  104  		}

  106  		// to when the resolved root is a main checkout that shares its
  107  		// index identity with one. relPath stays the repo-prefixed form
  108  		// for session bookkeeping — the prefix names the same repo
  109  		// regardless of which worktree the bytes land in.
  110  		abs = worktreeRootedPath(abs, root, s.multiIndexer)
  111  		return abs, rawPath, nil
  112  	}

  316      # appends to a hash a new value in a specified position so that the hash becomes:
  317      # { a: 1, b: 2, c: 3 } => append_hash(hash, :b, :d, 4) => { a: 1, b: 2, d: 4, c: 3 }
  318      # if key is not found then it will be inserted at the end
  319      def self.hash_append!(hash, after_key, key, value)
  320        insert_at = hash.to_a.index(hash.assoc(after_key))
  321        insert_at = insert_at.nil? ? hash.size : insert_at + 1
  322        hash.replace(hash.to_a.insert(insert_at, [key, value]).to_h)

  325      # prepends to a hash a new value in a specified position so that the hash becomes:

  327      # if key is not found then it will be inserted at the beggining
  328      def self.hash_prepend!(hash, before_key, key, value)
  329        insert_at = hash.to_a.index(hash.assoc(before_key))
